title: Geodrift traffic cushion and hotpatch procedure for cross-region failovers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Recent cross-region incidents revealed a recurring pattern we term 'geodrift' — gradual divergence between regional routing weight, capacity headroom, and KV-cache freshness which leads to elevated tail latency and customer-visible errors during traffic shifts. This ticket captures a production-safe runbook (soft-traffic cushion + verification probes) and a short-lived hotpatch plan for both Hosted and Dedicated customers to reduce blast radius during failovers and make emergency rollbacks deterministic.

Goals:
1) Provide an operator-run, tenant-safe traffic cushion that absorbs sudden weight shifts without dropping requests.
2) Define an automated verification probe sequence to assert KV cache alignment, model variant compatibility, and latency SLOs before finalizing a full regional cutover.
3) Ship a minimal hotpatch (runtime + routing guard) that can be applied to affected fleets within 15 minutes.
4) Codify escalation notes and customer communication templates for SE/CS teams.

Scope:
- Hosted: control-plane routing policies + runtime guards we can enable globally.
- Dedicated: tooling and a documented checklist for SREs and AE to safely apply per-tenant cushions (requires tenant ACL announcement for changes).

Trade-offs / Constraints:
- More aggressive cushions (longer soft-window) reduce risk but increase cross-region load and cost; will default to 3-minute cushion with exponential backoff tunable per-customer SLA.
- KV-cache reconciliation runs are IO-heavy; we prefer lazy reconciliation + per-tenant verification probes rather than mass pre-warm.
- Hotpatch is intentionally small to minimize regression risk; larger kernel/runtime changes must go through normal release with longer lead time.

Runbook (operator-facing) — short version:
1) Detect: Alert from region-latency spike + >10% dropped requests in region A (automatic trigger).
2) Isolate: Set region A to soft-evac mode (no hard rehome) — route up to 25% of traffic away gradually using traffic cushion.
3) Probe: Execute per-tenant verification probes against candidate region B: 10 short inference requests (varying seq lengths) + KV-read checks + model-variant hash validation.
4) Evaluate: If 95% probes succeed within 1.5x SLO and KV-staleness <= configured threshold, bump weight by 15% every 30s. Otherwise hold and notify eng on-call.
5) Hotpatch (if probes fail or KV desync detected): apply routing guard  (see PR link) to reject mismatched model variant requests and enable fallback route to regional cache origin.
6) Finalize: When traffic in new region stabilizes for 10 minutes and metrics show <1% error delta, complete rehome and schedule post-incident KV reconciliation job.

Hotpatch plan (code & deployment):
- Minimal changes in routing layer to add a short-lived guard flag (runtime flag) that enforces model-variant compatibility and drops stale-KV reads with a graceful retry to origin service.
- Target rollout: canary 2% across a warm fleet -> 20% -> 100% over 10 minutes with automated rollback on increased errors.
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/route-control/pull/3412 (routing-guard), https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7773 (guard hooks)

Customer escalation and comms:
- Template: brief incident summary, impacted regions, mitigation applied, ETA for full restoration, short-term workarounds. Link to support doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SE/pages/geo-failover-comm-template
- CS playbook: notify AE for Dedicated customers before applying per-tenant cushions; for Hosted customers, send post-factum summary + immediate next steps.

Testing and verification:
- Add end-to-end integration test to CI that simulates 30% weight shift and asserts probe success rate and cushion effect. Test branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/e2e-tests/compare/geodrift-cushion
- Add Grafana dashboards to show cushion progress, probe pass rates, KV-staleness distribution, and tenant error deltas.

Post-incident follow-ups (TO DOs):
- Add automated KV-staleness alerts (ENG-XXXXX)
- Expand canary probe scenarios to include large-seq and streaming cases
- Document Dedicated customer authorization flow for SRE hotpatch application

acceptance_criteria: Operator can execute runbook and complete a controlled regional rehome within 30 minutes with documented logs
Automated verification probes succeed >=95% for standard tenant workloads during cutover
Routing guard hotpatch can be rolled out and rolled back automatically within 15 minutes without increasing customer error-rate by >0.5%
CS/AE notified and sign-off recorded for Dedicated tenants before per-tenant actions
